scenes.heading: Data types
scenes.caption: Data types are the kinds of values a language can store. Numbers, text, true or false, collections, and “nothing” are the ones you meet first. Choosing the right type is how you tell the computer what operations are allowed, and how you tell a reader what a name means.

scenes.heading: Variables
scenes.caption: Variables are names for values. Each name is a label, and the value is whatever is stored under that label at this moment. Almost every program you write is a set of named values being changed on purpose. If the names are clear, the program is explainable.

scenes.heading: Recursion
scenes.caption: Recursion is a function that solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller version of the same problem, until it hits a base case that stops. It matches problems that contain smaller copies of themselves, such as folders inside folders, or a list you handle one item at a time.

items: Recursion is a function that solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller version of the same problem, until it hits a base case that stops
It matches problems that contain smaller copies of themselves, such as folders inside folders, or a list you handle one item at a time

scenes.heading: Step by step: Recursion
scenes.caption: Write the base case first. It must not call itself. Write the recursive case so the input gets strictly smaller. Trust the recursive call to return the answer for the smaller input. Combine that answer with the one item you kept.

items: Write the base case first. It must not call itself.
Write the recursive case so the input gets strictly smaller.
Trust the recursive call to return the answer for the smaller input.
Combine that answer with the one item you kept.

scenes.heading: Detail: Recursion
scenes.caption: If the input does not get smaller, the calls never end and the program runs out of stack space.

items: If the input does not get smaller, the calls never end and the program runs out of stack space.

scenes.heading: Detail: Recursion
scenes.caption: The base case is not optional. It is the whole reason the process stops.

items: The base case is not optional. It is the whole reason the process stops.

scenes.heading: Example: Recursion
scenes.caption: Here is a small example of Recursion. Read each line and say what it changes. def countdown(n):     if n == 0: return     print(n)     countdown(n - 1) countdown(3) prints 3, 2, 1 and stops. If you can change one piece and predict the new result, you have it.

lines: def countdown(n):
if n == 0: return
print(n)
countdown(n - 1)
countdown(3) prints 3, 2, 1 and stops.

scenes.heading: Pointers
scenes.caption: A pointer is a value that holds the address of another value. Following it is how you reach that other value. A null pointer points nowhere. Using a pointer that does not point at a live value is a crash or worse. Know who owns the memory and when it is freed.

items: A pointer is a value that holds the address of another value
Following it is how you reach that other value

Using a pointer that does not point at a live value is a crash or worse. Know who owns the memory and when it is freed

scenes.heading: Step by step: Pointers
scenes.caption: Take an address only of something that will live long enough. Check for null before you follow it. Free it once, in the owner, not in every reader. After free, do not use the pointer.

scenes.heading: pointers
scenes.caption: A pointer is a value that holds the address of another value. Following it is how you reach that other value. A null pointer points nowhere. Using a pointer that does not point at a live value is a crash or worse. Know who owns the memory and when it is freed.

items: A pointer is a value that holds the address of another value
Following it is how you reach that other value
A null pointer points nowhere
Using a pointer that does not point at a live value is a crash or worse. Know who owns the memory and when it is freed

scenes.heading: Step by step: pointers
scenes.caption: Take an address only of something that will live long enough. Check for null before you follow it. Free it once, in the owner, not in every reader. After free, do not use the pointer.

items: Take an address only of something that will live long enough.
Check for null before you follow it.
Free it once, in the owner, not in every reader.
After free, do not use the pointer.

scenes.heading: Stack
scenes.caption: A stack is a collection where the last item you put in is the first item you take out. Push adds. Pop removes the most recent. Function calls, undo buttons, and matching brackets are all stacks. The most recent open thing closes first.

items: A stack is a collection where the last item you put in is the first item you take out

Pop removes the most recent
Function calls, undo buttons, and matching brackets are all stacks. The most recent open thing closes first

scenes.heading: Step by step: Stack
scenes.caption: Push items as you open them. Pop when you close the most recent one. Peek if you need to look without removing. Popping an empty stack is an error. Guard it.

items: Push items as you open them.
Pop when you close the most recent one.

Popping an empty stack is an error. Guard it.
